english.title: Enter United Kingdom without a passport for a dependent child

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Asylum and Immigration Treatment of Claimants

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) at a leave or asylum interview failed to have with you in respect of a dependent child, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHILD'S NAME..), with whom you claimed to be travelling or living, an immigration document which was in force and satisfactorily established the child's identity and nationality or citizenship
english.legislation: Contrary to section 2(2) and (9) of the Asylum and Immigration (Treatment of Claimants, etc.) Act 2004.

english.notes:
Subsection 2(3) and (5) of the Act provide:-.
2(3) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if:-
(a) the interview referred to in that subsection takes place after the person has entered the United Kingdom, and (b) within the period of three days beginning with the date of the interview the person provides to an immigration officer or to the Secretary of State a document of the kind referred to in that subsection.

2(5) of the Act provides that it is a defence for a person in respect of a child:-
(a) to prove that the child is an EEA national,
(b) to prove that the child is a member of the family of an EEA national and that the child is exercising a right under the Community Treaties in respect of entry to or residence in the United Kingdom,
(c) to prove that the person has a reasonable excuse for not being in possession of a document of the kind specified in subsection (2),
(d) to produce a false immigration document and to prove that it was used as an immigration document for all purposes in connection with the child's journey to the United Kingdom, or
(e) to prove that he travelled to the United Kingdom with the child without, at any stage since he set out on the journey, having possession of an immigration document in respect of the child.
(f) The fact that a document was deliberately destroyed or disposed of is not a reasonable excuse unless it can be shown that this was for a reasonable cause or beyond the control of the person.
(g) Reasonable cause does not include for the purposes of delaying the handling or resolution of a claim, increasing the chances of success of a claim or application or complying with the instructions or advice given by an agent or facilitator (unless in the circumstances it would be unreasonable to expect non-compliance).

other.powersofarrest: Section 2(10) provides:- "If a constable or immigration officer reasonably suspects that a person has committed an offence under this section he may arrest the person without warrant".
other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 154 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (c. 44) (increased limit on magistrates' power of imprisonment), sentencing shall have the effect as if the reference to twelve months were a reference to six months.

Time limit on prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
